Public Design Commission Outdoor Public.query: Retrieve all outdoor artworks from the Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory where the material is specified, including their latitude, longitude, address, and creation year Using the creation year of each artwork, classify each artwork into a time category of recent, mid‑century, or historic Group artworks by the combination of latitude, longitude, address, and creation year, and count how many artworks exist at each such combination for those with specified material For each unique combination of latitude, longitude, address, and creation year where material is specified, calculate basic statistics on the creation years of artworks at that location, including the average creation year, the total (sum) of creation years, and the most recent creation year
Public Design Commission Outdoor Public.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT t1.latitude AS t1_latitude,
         t1.longitude AS t1_longitude,
         t1.address AS t1_address,
         t3.latitude,
         t3.longitude,
         t4.address,
         t3.date_created,
         t4.artwork_type1,
         t5.material,
         CASE
           WHEN t3.date_created > 2000 THEN 'recent'
           WHEN t3.date_created > 1950 THEN 'mid_century'
           ELSE 'historic'
         END AS category
  FROM `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory` t2 ON t1.title = t2.title
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_artworks_1` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory_2` t4 ON t1.address = t4.address
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_artworks` t5 ON t2.acquisition = t5.acquisition
  WHERE t5.material IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT t1_latitude,
       t1_longitude,
       t1_address,
       date_created,
       category,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(date_created) AS avg_value,
       SUM(date_created) AS total_value,
       MAX(date_created) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY t1_latitude,
         t1_longitude,
         t1_address,
         date_created,
         category

    t2.code1,
    t4.code1 AS t4_code1,

)

  t4_code1,

  fax_number,

NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical).sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.building_manager AS t1_building_manager,
    t3.building_manager AS t3_building_manager,
    t1.total_gallons_high,
    t3.city_council_district,
    t3.total_units,
    t5.of_res_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN t1.total_gallons_high > 150000 THEN 'very_high_usage'
      WHEN t1.total_gallons_high > 50000 THEN 'high_usage'
      ELSE 'moderate_or_low_usage'
    END AS category
  FROM `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data` t2 ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application

  WHERE t3.total_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t1_building_manager,
  t3_building_manager,
  city_council_district,
  total_units,
  of_res_units,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(total_gallons_high) AS avg_value,
  SUM(total_gallons_high) AS total_value,
  MAX(total_gallons_high) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  t1_building_manager,
  t3_building_manager,
  city_council_district,
  total_units,
  of_res_units,
  category

    dep_boiler_application,

WHERE total > 0

Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.vehicle_year,
    t2.vehicle_color,
    t3.violation_precinct,
    t3.days_parking_in_effect,
    t4.issuing_agency,
    t4.plate_type,
    t5.issue_date,
    t5.violation_description,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.violation_precinct 
      ORDER BY t2.vehicle_year DESC
    ) AS row_num
  FROM `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2017_parking_violations_2017` t1
  INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2017_parking_violations_2017_1` t2 ON t1.summons_number = t2.summons_number
  INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2017_parking_violation_records_2017` t3 ON t1.plate_id = t3.plate_id
  INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2017_parking_violations_fy2017` t4 ON t1.street_name = t4.street_name
  INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2017_parking_violations_2017_2` t5 ON t1.issuer_code = t5.issuer_code
  WHERE t5.issue_date >= '2017-01-01'
)
SELECT 
  vehicle_year,
  vehicle_color,
  violation_precinct,
  days_parking_in_effect,
  issuing_agency,
  plate_type,
  issue_date,
  violation_description
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

Speed Reducer Tracking System (SRTS).query: List speed reducer installations in the SRTS program with their installation dates and associated segment identifiers Retrieve work order or tracking numbers associated with each speed reducer installation Get the request segment status description for each segment associated with a speed reducer installation Get the status code from the related request record for each speed reducer installation Retrieve the internal location or boro street code for each speed reducer installation Retrieve the street name for each speed reducer installation Determine the installation rank of each speed reducer within its segment based on installation date Determine the installation order rank of each speed reducer within its street based on installation date Filter to the five most recently installed speed reducers per segment

WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.segmentid,
    t1.oft,
    t1.installationdate,
    t2.segmentid AS t2_segmentid,

    t4.oft AS t4_oft,
    t4.segmentstatus,
    t5.tolongitude AS t5_tolongitude,
    t5.bctsnum,
    t6.onstreet,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t2.segmentid ORDER BY t1.installationdate DESC) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t6.onstreet ORDER BY t1.installationdate) AS dense_rank
  FROM `Speed Reducer Tracking System (SRTS)_speed_reducer_projects_status` t1
  INNER JOIN `Speed Reducer Tracking System (SRTS)_speed_reducer_requests` t2 ON t1.segmentid = t2.segmentid

  INNER JOIN `Speed Reducer Tracking System (SRTS)_speed_reducer_status` t6 ON t3.tolatitude = t6.tolatitude
)
SELECT

  oft,
  t2_segmentid,
  tolongitude,
  t4_oft,
  bctsnum,
  onstreet,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

Vision Zero Base Report.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT t1.license_number AS t1_license_number,
       t2.license_number AS t2_license_number,
       t1.phone AS t1_phone,
       t3.phone AS t3_phone,
       t1.average_vehicle_age,
       t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
       t3.fatal_crashes
FROM `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_statistics` t1
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_taxi_base_safety_data` t2 ON t1.license_number = t2.license_number
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_and_accessibility_data` t4 ON t2.location = t4.location
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_reports` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
WHERE t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT t1_license_number,
       t2_license_number,
       t1_phone,
       t3_phone,
       percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
       COUNT(*) as record_count,
       SUM(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as total_amount,
       AVG(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as avg_amount,
       MAX(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as max_amount,
       MIN(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as min_amount
FROM base_data
GROUP BY t1_license_number,
         t2_license_number,
         t1_phone,
         t3_phone,

DSNY DonateNYC Directory.query: Find donation locations that have published operating hours and accept the specified types of donations For each qualifying donation location, retrieve its name For each qualifying donation location, retrieve the kinds of items they accept For each qualifying donation location, retrieve the state senate district they are in Compute the combined district number for each qualifying donation location Rank donation locations by combined district number and select the top 50 For each of the top 50 donation locations, count how many matching records were found for that location
DSNY DonateNYC Directory.sql:
WITH raw_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.objectid,
    t1.latitude,
    t1.longitude,
    t1.address,
    t2.objectid AS t2_objectid,
    t2.site,
    t3.latitude AS t3_latitude,
    t3.longitude AS t3_longitude,
    t3.phone,
    t4.bin,
    t4.address AS t4_address,
    t5.site AS t5_site,
    t5.categoriesaccepted,
    t6.phone AS t6_phone,
    t6.hours,
    t7.bin AS t7_bin,
    t7.email,
    t5.senate_district
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory_1` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_1` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_center_locations` t4 ON t1.address = t4.address
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_sites_directory` t5 ON t2.site = t5.site
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory_2` t6 ON t3.phone = t6.phone
  INNER JOIN `DSNY DonateNYC Directory_donation_centers_directory` t7 ON t4.bin = t7.bin
  WHERE t5.categoriesaccepted IS NOT NULL
), filtered AS (
  SELECT 
    objectid,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    address,
    t2_objectid,
    site,
    t3_latitude,
    t3_longitude,
    phone,
    bin,
    t4_address,
    t5_site,
    categoriesaccepted,
    t6_phone,
    hours,
    t7_bin,
    email,
    senate_district
  FROM raw_data
  WHERE hours IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    site,
    categoriesaccepted,
    senate_district,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    SUM(senate_district) AS total
  FROM filtered
  GROUP BY site, categoriesaccepted, senate_district
)
SELECT 
  site,
  categoriesaccepted,
  senate_district,
  count,
  total
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY total DESC

    t3.fixed_address,
    t3.state_senate_district,
    t4.city,
    t4.site_budget,
    t5.service_taxonomy,
    t6.serves_food,

      WHEN t4.site_budget > 100000 THEN 'Medium Budget'

    END as category
  FROM `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites` t1
  INNER JOIN `Verified Locations for NYC City-Funded Social Service Contracts - Sites_nyc_social_service_sites_3` t2 ON t1.site_id = t2.site_id

)

  city,

  SUM(site_budget) as total_value,
  MAX(site_budget) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY

  service_taxonomy,
  serves_food,
  category

2019 DOE High School Directory.query: Find the total attendance across all records for each high school program and identify the top 50 programs by this total attendance where the average student attendance is above 90% For each of the selected top 50 high school programs, retrieve the program’s identifying code For each of the selected top 50 high school programs, retrieve both listed contact phone numbers and indicate when they differ For each of the selected top 50 high school programs, retrieve the percentage of students reporting how safe they feel at the program For each of the selected top 50 high school programs, retrieve the number of 9th-grade applicants received
2019 DOE High School Directory.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.code1,
    t2.phone_number,
    t5.phone_number AS t5_phone_number,
    t6.code1 AS t6_code1,
    t4.pct_stu_safe,
    t5.grade9geapplicants10,
    t6.attendance_rate
  FROM `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2019` t1
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  INNER JOIN `2019 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t6 ON t3.code1 = t6.code1
  WHERE t6.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    code1,
    phone_number,
    t5_phone_number,
    t6_code1,
    SUM(attendance_rate) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(attendance_rate) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number, t6_code1
)
SELECT 
  code1,
  phone_number,
  t5_phone_number,
  t6_code1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE average > 0.9
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

INNER JOIN `2021 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL) SELECT dbn, t2_dbn, school_name, t3_school_name, code1, t4_code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number, COUNT(*) as record_count, SUM(pct_stu_safe) as total_amount, AVG(pct_stu_safe) as avg_amount, MAX(pct_stu_safe) as max_amount, MIN(pct_stu_safe) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY dbn, t2_dbn, school_name, t3_school_name, code1, t4_code1, phone_number, t5_phone_number HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
SELECT t3.prevailing_wage_status,
       t3.other_income_units,
       t3._2_br_units,
       t5.project_name,
       t5.total_units,
       t5.middle_income_units,

WHERE t5.total_units IS NOT NULL

Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.query: List all building locations with their associated properties and the size group of each property For each building location and size group, count how many properties fall into that size group For each building location, calculate the average number of housing units For each building location, calculate the total number of housing units For each building location, find the largest (maximum) number of housing units in any single property Identify, for each building location, the count of main counted housing units that are available Identify, for each building location, the count of housing units reserved for other income levels Compare, for each building location, the main counted available units with the units reserved for other income levels
Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude, 
    t1.longitude, 
    t3.latitude AS t3_latitude, 
    t3.longitude AS t3_longitude, 
    t1.all_counted_units, 
    t3.other_income_units, 
    t5.total_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.total_units > 100 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t5.total_units > 50 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END AS category
  FROM `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_units_by_building` t2 ON t1.building_id = t2.building_id
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings_1` t4 ON t2.house_number = t4.house_number
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings` t5 ON t4.project_id = t5.project_id
  WHERE t1.all_counted_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t1_latitude AS latitude,
  t1_longitude AS longitude,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(total_units) AS avg_value,
  SUM(total_units) AS total_value,
  MAX(total_units) AS max_value
FROM (
  SELECT 
    latitude AS t1_latitude,
    longitude AS t1_longitude,
    t3_latitude,
    t3_longitude,
    all_counted_units,
    other_income_units,
    total_units,
    category
  FROM categorized_data
) AS categorized_data
GROUP BY t1_latitude, t1_longitude, category

Facilities Database.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT t3.facgroup,
         t3.xcoord,
         t3.overagency,
         t4.overlevel,
         t4.ycoord,
         t5.schooldist,
         t5.factype,
         t5.datasource,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.schooldist ORDER BY t4.ycoord DESC) AS row_num
  FROM `Facilities Database_facility_locations_info_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Facilities Database_facility_locations_info` t2 ON t1.uid = t2.uid

DOB ECB Violations.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.dob_violation_number,
    t3.issue_date,
    t4.respondent_city,
    t5.respondent_house_number,
    t5.ecb_violation_status,
    t6.violation_description,
    t6.penality_imposed,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.penality_imposed > 10000 THEN 'High Penalty'
      WHEN t6.penality_imposed > 1000 THEN 'Medium Penalty'
      ELSE 'Low Penalty'
    END as category
  FROM `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records_3` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records_1` t2 ON t1.ecb_violation_number = t2.ecb_violation_number

  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_dob_ecb_violation_records` t5 ON t1.bin = t5.bin
  INNER JOIN `DOB ECB Violations_building_violation_records` t6 ON t2.block = t6.block
  WHERE t6.penality_imposed IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  dob_violation_number,
  issue_date,
  respondent_city,
  ecb_violation_status,
  violation_description,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(penality_imposed) as avg_value,
  SUM(penality_imposed) as total_value,
  MAX(penality_imposed) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  dob_violation_number,
  issue_date,
  respondent_city,
  ecb_violation_status,
  violation_description,
  category

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT t3.trailerstate,
         t3.endzipcode,
         t3.truckyear,
         t3.totalgrossweight,
         t5.applicationdate,
         t5.endcity,

         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.trailerstate ORDER BY t5.applicationdate DESC) AS row_num

)
SELECT trailerstate,

       truckyear,
       totalgrossweight,
       applicationdate,
       endcity,
       overallwidth

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:

         CASE
           WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 160000 THEN 'Very Heavy'

           ELSE 'Standard'
         END AS category
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1

  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t5.overallwidth > 8.0
)

       AVG(totalgrossweight) AS avg_value,
       SUM(totalgrossweight) AS total_value,
       MAX(totalgrossweight) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY fullpermitno, category

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: List all trailers and identify each trailer's home state Retrieve all permits associated with each trailer, including vehicle width and permit application date Find the top five permits per trailer home state with the greatest vehicle width For each selected permit, retrieve the trip end location details (city and ZIP) For each selected permit, retrieve the trip start location details (state and ZIP) For each selected permit, determine the truck's age at the time of permit application (using truck manufacture date and permit application date) For each selected permit, compute how its vehicle width ranks against all other permits within the same trailer home state For each selected permit, compute how its vehicle width ranks against all other permits within the same trip starting state
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.trailerstate,
    t3.endzipcode,
    t3.truckyear,
    t4.applicationdate,
    t4.startzipcode,
    t4.startstate,
    t5.applicationdate,
    t5.endcity,
    t5.overallwidth,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.trailerstate 
      ORDER BY t5.overallwidth DESC
    ) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t4.startstate 
      ORDER BY t3.truckyear
    ) AS dense_rank
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endzipcode,
  truckyear,
  applicationdate,
  startzipcode,
  startstate,
  endcity,
  overallwidth,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid

INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate GROUP BY t4.applicationdate, t5.applicationdate, t3.trailerstate, t3.totalgrossweight, t4.loadlength, t5.overallwidth

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Find the most recent five permits issued since the start of 2023 Retrieve the permit numbers for these permits Retrieve the application dates for these permits Retrieve the load weights for these permits Retrieve the total vehicle-plus-load weights for these permits Retrieve the load lengths for these permits Retrieve the load heights for these permits Retrieve the destination city where each trip was supposed to end for these permits
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (

  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
SELECT t1.fullpermitno, SUM(t1.loadweight) AS total_loadweight, t3.totalgrossweight, t4.applicationdate, t5.applicationdate FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: List all permit applications with their matching reference numbers Find the original application date for each permit application Find the linked application date for each permit application Find the state where the trailer was registered for each permit application Find the destination city associated with each permit application Determine how many moves fall into each weight category for each permit application Calculate the average loaded weight of moves for each permit application Calculate the total loaded weight of moves for each permit application Find the heaviest overall loaded weight of moves for each permit application
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.fullapplicationno AS t2_fullapplicationno,
    t4.fullapplicationno,
    t4.applicationdate,
    t5.applicationdate AS t5_applicationdate,
    t3.trailerstate,
    t5.endcity,
    t3.totalgrossweight,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 160000 THEN 'very_heavy'
      WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 120000 THEN 'heavy'
      ELSE 'standard'
    END AS category
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t3.totalgrossweight IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t2_fullapplicationno,
  fullapplicationno,
  applicationdate,
  t5_applicationdate,
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(totalgrossweight) AS avg_value,
  SUM(totalgrossweight) AS total_value,
  MAX(totalgrossweight) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  t2_fullapplicationno,
  fullapplicationno,
  applicationdate,
  t5_applicationdate,
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  category

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: List each permit application For each permit application, find how many permits are tied to it For each permit application, find when it was submitted For each permit application, find the state the trailer was registered in For each permit application, find which city the trip ended in

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Retrieve oversize vehicle permits issued since the start of 2023 Determine the city and state for each oversize vehicle permit issued since the start of 2023 Calculate the total number of oversize vehicle permits per city and state combination since the start of 2023 Calculate the total combined width of oversize vehicle loads per city and state combination since the start of 2023 Calculate the average width per oversize vehicle permit per city and state combination since the start of 2023 Rank city and state combinations by permit-related width metrics and identify the top 100
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT 
  t1.permitid,
  t1.fullpermitno,
  t2.permitid AS t2_permitid,
  t2.fullapplicationno,
  t4.fullapplicationno AS t4_fullapplicationno,
  t4.applicationdate,
  t3.fullpermitno AS t3_fullpermitno,
  t3.trailerstate,
  t5.applicationdate,
  t5.endcity,
  t5.overallwidth
FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
WHERE t5.applicationdate >= '2023-01-01') ,
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    trailerstate,
    endcity,
    SUM(overallwidth) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(overallwidth) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY trailerstate, endcity
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE count >= 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

WITH categorized_data AS (

WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.geocode,
    t4.geocode AS t4_geocode,
    t4.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t5.latitude AS t5_latitude,
    t5.longitude AS t5_longitude,

    t5.nocrim_n,

    END as category
  FROM `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_statistics` t1

  INNER JOIN `2016 - 2017 School Safety Report_school_safety_metrics` t3 ON t1.location_code = t3.location_code

)

  geocode,
  t4_geocode,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  t5_latitude,
  t5_longitude,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(nocrim_n) as avg_value,
  SUM(nocrim_n) as total_value,
  MAX(nocrim_n) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  geocode,
  t4_geocode,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  t5_latitude,
  t5_longitude,
  category

  INNER JOIN `Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_payments` t2 ON t1.payment_id = t2.payment_id
  INNER JOIN `Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_usage_1` t3 ON t1.contract_id_ = t3.contract_id_

  INNER JOIN `Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_projects` t5 ON t4.contract_name = t5.contract_name
  WHERE t1.project_status IS NOT NULL
)

Historical DOB Permit Issuance.query: Retrieve all Historical DOB Permit Issuance records where permit type is present Determine for each permit whether the associated project is residential or not Identify the type of work associated with each permit Classify each permit into low, medium, or high volume categories based on its permit sequence number Link permit records using job number to ensure correct aggregation across related tables Link permit records using building ID to ensure correct aggregation across related building information Link permit records using latitude and longitude to ensure location-based consistency in the dataset Link permit records using owner contact details to ensure correct association with property owner information Calculate, for each combination of permit type, residential status, work type, and volume category, the total count of permits Calculate, for each combination of permit type, residential status, work type, and volume category, the average permit sequence number Calculate, for each combination of permit type, residential status, work type, and volume category, the total (sum) of permit sequence numbers Calculate, for each combination of permit type, residential status, work type, and volume category, the highest permit sequence number
Historical DOB Permit Issuance.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.site_fill,
    t4.permit_type,
    t5.residential,
    t6.work_type,
    t6.permit_sequence,
    t6.special_district_1,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.permit_sequence > 1000 THEN 'high volume'
      WHEN t6.permit_sequence > 100 THEN 'medium volume'
      ELSE 'low volume'
    END as category
  FROM `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_building_permit_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_dob_permit_issuance_records_1` t2 ON t1.job = t2.job
  INNER JOIN `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_permit_issuance_records` t3 ON t1.bin = t3.bin
  INNER JOIN `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_dob_permit_issuance_records_2` t4 ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_dob_permit_issuance_records` t5 ON t2.owner_s_phone = t5.owner_s_phone
  INNER JOIN `Historical DOB Permit Issuance_permit_issuance_records_1` t6 ON t2.owner_s_last_name = t6.owner_s_last_name
  WHERE t4.permit_type IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  permit_type,
  residential,
  work_type,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(permit_sequence) as avg_value,
  SUM(permit_sequence) as total_value,
  MAX(permit_sequence) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  permit_type,
  residential,
  work_type,
  category

Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS).query: Find all completed buildings and their general north–south locations in the city, along with their street numbers and associated tax lots For each completed building, find all public spaces associated with that building For each public space, determine its type For each public space, determine whether it is accessible to people with physical disabilities For each public space, retrieve its northing value For each public space type and accessibility status within each general north–south location, calculate the count of public spaces For each general north–south location, calculate the average, total, and highest northing value of its public spaces For each public space (or building group, as applicable), retrieve the minimum required size For each public space or building record included in the results, retrieve the tax lot and street number of the building where the public space is located
Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS).sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t3.size_required, t3.building_constructed, t4.tax_lot, t4.ycoordinate, t5.physically_disabled, t6.address_number, t6.public_space_type, CASE WHEN t4.ycoordinate > 220000 THEN 'High Y' WHEN t4.ycoordinate > 210000 THEN 'Medium Y' ELSE 'Low Y' END as category FROM `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_public_spaces_access_info` t1
INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_public_spaces_nyc` t2 ON t1.pops_number = t2.pops_number

INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_pops_location_data` t4 ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_pops_accessibility_info` t5 ON t2.bin = t5.bin
INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_public_space_locations` t6 ON t2.building_location = t6.building_location WHERE t3.building_constructed = 'Completed') SELECT building_constructed, physically_disabled, public_space_type, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(ycoordinate) as avg_value, SUM(ycoordinate) as total_value, MAX(ycoordinate) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY building_constructed, physically_disabled, public_space_type, category

INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_pops_location_data` t4 ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_pops_accessibility_info` t5 ON t2.bin = t5.bin
INNER JOIN `Privately Owned Public Spaces (POPS)_public_space_locations` t6 ON t2.building_location = t6.building_location WHERE t1.latitude IS NOT NULL AND t4.latitude IS NOT NULL AND t4.longitude IS NOT NULL AND t3.building_address_with_zip IS NOT NULL AND t1.longitude IS NOT NULL AND t1.building_address_with_zip IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (SELECT building_address_with_zip, t3_building_address_with_zip, latitude, longitude, t4_latitude, t4_longitude, SUM(address_number) as total, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(address_number) as average FROM base_data GROUP BY building_address_with_zip, t3_building_address_with_zip, latitude, longitude, t4_latitude, t4_longitude) SELECT building_address_with_zip, t3_building_address_with_zip, latitude, longitude, t4_latitude, t4_longitude, total, count, average FROM aggregated WHERE total > 0 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 100

WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.facility_name, 
    t3.address_1, 
    t3.current_total_ghg_emissions, 
    t4.facility_name AS facility_name_t4, 
    t4.current_site_pdu_input_energy,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.current_total_ghg_emissions > 10000 THEN 'High Emissions'
      WHEN t3.current_total_ghg_emissions > 5000 THEN 'Medium Emissions'
      ELSE 'Low Emissions'
    END as category
  FROM `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2012 (Data for Calendar Year 2011)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2011` t1
  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2012 (Data for Calendar Year 2011)_nyc_building_energy_water_2011` t2 ON t1.building_id_espm = t2.building_id_espm
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.address_1 = t3.address_1
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t2.facility_name = t4.facility_name 
  WHERE t3.current_total_ghg_emissions IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  facility_name, 
  facility_name_t4, 
  address_1, 
  category, 
  COUNT(*) as count, 
  AVG(current_total_ghg_emissions) as avg_value, 
  SUM(current_total_ghg_emissions) as total_value, 
  MAX(current_total_ghg_emissions) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  facility_name, 
  facility_name_t4, 
  address_1, 
  category

), aggregated AS (

)
